TORONTO HOUSING — COMPLETE PC HANDOFF
Prepared October 27, 2026

1. Download and extract the entire ZIP on your PC before opening files.
2. Read CONTINUE IN CHATGPT.txt, then upload that file, the final slides PDF, the Excel workbook and the graph explanation document to a new ChatGPT chat. If ChatGPT accepts ZIP uploads, you can upload this entire package instead.
3. To view the portfolio draft, open 02 - Portfolio Case Study Draft/index.html in Chrome or Edge. Keep its assets folder and style.css beside it. Internet access helps load the optional DM Sans font; local fallback fonts work offline.
4. The Tableau .twbx includes its data. Open it in a compatible Tableau Desktop version to edit. The final PDF and chart images can be viewed without Tableau.
5. Supply the CORRECT existing portfolio URL/source and brand guide to your new chat before asking it to integrate after TSTAR. These were not established in this session.

FOLDERS
01 - Final Project: final slides, cleaned Excel, graph explanations (Word and PDF), packaged Tableau workbook.
02 - Portfolio Case Study Draft: editable HTML/CSS, local assets, SVG map and dot chart, original presentation and 2011 CSV.
03 - Source Data: cleaned 2011 table and map geometry, separate 2016 table and map geometry, illustrative budgets.
04 - Chart Images: individual chart PNGs plus the final Tableau map and scatterplot exports.
05 - Sketchbook Reference Only: existing retrieved portfolio snapshot, not confirmed as your intended portfolio. Its JavaScript is saved as .js.txt for email compatibility.

STATUS
The visual case study is a local draft. No live portfolio was modified or deployed. All draft asset links and 140 neighbourhood records were checked. Browser visual QA remains pending because the in-app browser could not reach the local preview. The draft temporarily uses the retrieved Sketchbook visual style; the intended brand guide is still needed.

The project uses historical 2011 and 2016 data. It is not a current rental-market report. The two years describe different populations and must not be presented as a direct trend.
